military.t: IRGC FIRED ON INDIAN SHIPS IN HORMUZ — VLCC Attacked Despite Clearance
military.d: UKMTO confirmed: "The Master of the Tanker reports being approached by 2 IRGC gun boats, no VHF challenge, that then fires upon the tanker. The tanker and crew are reported safe." Two Indian vessels were forced back west after IRGC gunboats opened fire (Republic World, TankerTrackers.com). One vessel was an Indian-flagged VLCC supertanker carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude oil — attacked DESPITE having received clearance from Iranian port authorities to transit. Republic TV has exclusive audio of the mayday call made by the captain immediately after being fired upon. At least 3 attacks total (US defense official to Axios), 2 attacks confirmed by UKMTO. One ship hit, some damage, no injuries reported. Four Indian and two Greek tankers also failed to cross.

military.t: HORMUZ RECLOSED — Iran IRIB: Returned to Previous State
military.d: Iran IRIB state TV, quoting IRGC Armed Forces spokesperson: the Strait of Hormuz "has returned to its previous state." Iran's IRGC accused the US of "continuing piracy and maritime robbery under the so-called blockade" and said the US failed to uphold commitments. Iran said it previously allowed "managed passage of a limited number of oil tankers and commercial vessels in good faith following recent negotiations" — but US continuing blockade meant conditions not met. The Hormuz opening declared by FM Araghchi on April 17 lasted less than 24 hours. This is the most severe single-day reversal in the war's diplomatic trajectory.

military.t: INDIA SUMMONS IRANIAN AMBASSADOR — Bilateral Diplomatic Crisis
military.d: India summoned the Iranian Ambassador to the MEA following the IRGC attack on two Indian-flagged vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. India lodged a strong protest. The attacked Indian VLCC was carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude oil — one of the largest commercial tankers in the Gulf. The captain had received explicit clearance from Iranian port authorities before IRGC gunboats opened fire without any radio challenge. This is a direct attack on Indian-flagged vessels and Indian crew. India-Iran relations had been on careful footing since Iran gave India special transit rights in March (along with China, Russia, Pakistan, Iraq). Those preferential arrangements appear to have broken down. Op Urja Suraksha on high alert.

military.t: TRUMP: "Iran Got a Little Cute." Still Talking — Knows by End of Day.
military.d: Trump, speaking to reporters in the Oval Office Saturday: Iran "got a little cute, they wanted to close up the Strait again" and the US "can't blackmail us." Said the US is still talking to Iran and he expects to know by end of day whether parties will move forward with a deal. Crucially — Trump did NOT walk away. His framing suggests he views this as a negotiating escalation rather than a full breakdown. "They got a little cute" implies tactical irritation, not strategic abandonment. Second round Islamabad talks remain uncertain but not officially cancelled. US CENTCOM: 23 ships total have now turned around since blockade began.

military.t: The 24-Hour Hormuz Sequence — What Actually Happened
military.d: Apr 17 morning: FM Araghchi declares Hormuz completely open for all commercial vessels. Apr 17 evening: Ghalibaf posts on X — Hormuz will close if US does not lift blockade. Apr 18 morning: Ships attempt transit believing FM opening is in effect. Some received explicit clearance from Iranian port authorities. Apr 18 mid-morning: IRGC gunboats approach ships WITHOUT VHF challenge and open fire. Iran IRIB announces Hormuz returned to previous state. Iran says US continuing blockade = conditions not met. The clearance given by port authorities and the IRGC action appear uncoordinated — Iranian civilian port authority vs IRGC military command acting independently. This is the most dangerous internal Iran incoherence since the war began.

military.t: Rubio April 18: Iran CAN Have Civilian Nuclear Program — Position Shift Stands
military.d: Despite the Hormuz crisis, Rubio's April 18 statement that Iran can have a civilian nuclear energy program remains on the record — the most significant US concession of the war. This creates a deal framework even as Hormuz tensions escalate. The Hormuz crisis is a negotiating tactic (similar to US announcing blockade Apr 13 after Islamabad talks failed) — both sides using maximum pressure while keeping diplomatic channel open. Pakistan continuing to mediate. If Trump knows by end of day that deal is on, talks could proceed Sunday despite crisis. The Rubio civilian-nuclear concession is the key unlocking condition for a final deal.

military.t: Monday April 21: Ceasefire Expiry + Market Open — The Critical Day
military.d: Monday April 21 is simultaneously the day India markets open and the day the US-Iran ceasefire expires. The weekend's entire sequence — Hormuz opened, IRGC fired on Indian ships, Hormuz reclosed — will be fully priced in on Monday morning. Scenario A (~45%): Deal/extension announced over weekend despite Hormuz crisis → Sensex gap-up, Brent falls → LPG cut approaching. assessment.body:
Day 50 is the most volatile 24-hour period since the war began on February 28.

THE HORMUZ SEQUENCE — WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED TODAY
• Apr 17 AM: FM Araghchi declares Hormuz "completely open" for all commercial vessels
• Apr 17 PM: Ghalibaf posts Iran will close Hormuz if US does not lift blockade
• Apr 18 AM: Ships attempt transit. Some receive explicit clearance from Iranian port authorities
• Apr 18 MID-MORNING: 2 IRGC gunboats approach ships without VHF radio challenge → open fire
• UKMTO confirmed: tanker captain reports "2 IRGC gun boats, no VHF challenge, then fires"
• Crew reported safe. One ship hit — some damage, no injuries
• Apr 18: Iran IRIB — Hormuz "returned to its previous state"
• Iran: US continuing "piracy and maritime robbery" = conditions for opening not met
• The FM opening and IRGC action appear to be UNCOORDINATED — civilian vs military chain of command

INDIA DIRECTLY HIT — THE MOST SERIOUS BILATERAL INCIDENT OF THE WAR
• TWO Indian-flagged vessels fired upon — forced back west
• Indian VLCC carrying 2 MILLION BARRELS of Iraqi crude oil attacked
• Attacked DESPITE having clearance from Iranian port authorities
• Captain made mayday call — audio captured by Republic TV
• 4 additional Indian tankers + 2 Greek tankers also failed to cross
• India summoned Iranian Ambassador — strong protest lodged
• Op Urja Suraksha on HIGH ALERT — Indian Navy warships in Gulf of Oman
• This is a direct attack on Indian crew, Indian cargo, Indian flag

WHAT TRUMP SAID — NO WALKAWAY YET
• Oval Office Saturday: "Iran got a little cute, wanted to close up the Strait again"
• "Can't blackmail us" — but added: "We're still talking"
• Will know "by end of day" if deal going forward
• This is NOT a negotiating breakdown language — it's pressure management
• Rubio's civilian-nuclear concession from this morning still stands
• Pakistan still mediating — both sides technically still "in contact"

INDIA MARKET OUTLOOK — MONDAY APRIL 21
• Markets closed Saturday-Sunday. Next open: Monday April 21 = CEASEFIRE EXPIRY DAY
• This is the most consequential market open since February 28
• If deal/extension announced this weekend DESPITE crisis: gap-up toward 78,000-79,000
• If Hormuz stays closed + ceasefire lapses without deal: gap-down 75,000-76,000
• Brent currently spiking from Friday's $88-90 back toward $95-100 range
• LPG price cut scenario: REVERSED until Hormuz reopens sustainably
• India VIX will spike Monday — expect high volatility all session

CEASEFIRE: APRIL 22 — 4 DAYS REMAINING
• Scenario A (~40%): Crisis is negotiating theatre → deal/extension announced Sunday → Brent $75-80, Sensex 80,000+
• Scenario B (~35%): Hormuz stays closed, ceasefire lapses Apr 22 → Brent $115-125, Sensex 64,000-67,000
• Scenario C (~25%): Emergency ceasefire extension, Hormuz partial → Sensex 77,000-79,000, Brent $90-95

WHAT TO WATCH TONIGHT AND TOMORROW
• Trump announcement on deal status — expected "by end of day" Saturday
• Iran FM or official response to IRGC actions — did Araghchi sanction IRGC firing?
• Whether second round talks confirmed for Sunday in Islamabad
• Brent price movement — sustained above $95 = full LPG crisis reversal
• India MEA formal statement and whether Iran responds to ambassador summons

VERDICT: The Iran civilian-military coordination breakdown — port authorities granting clearance while IRGC fires — is the most dangerous new development since the blockade. India is directly targeted. But Trump's language ("still talking") and the Rubio concession suggest both sides want a deal. The next 24 hours determine whether this is the last pressure play before a deal or the beginning of a new escalation cycle.
